name: Medpace Holdings, Inc.
moat_justification: Integrated full-service CRO model with real mid-trial switching friction, deep scientific/regulatory expertise and ~21% operating margins vs ~15-18% peer EBITDA margins, but project-based contracts, ~5% share vs IQVIA/ICON scale, top-5 client concentration ~31% of revenue, and a funding-sensitive small-biotech customer base cap durability. Reported roic_proxy breaks in recent years (buybacks shrank equity below cash, driving invested capital toward zero); the margin series is the usable return evidence.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 4.3%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight

DEBT_TAGS_BLANK: no debt tag reports for the latest fiscal year — net debt is UNKNOWN (not zero); no leverage verdict is possible from the engine, state the balance sheet from the filing in analysis.md
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.9x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (8.6%) vs bull-case tier C (13.6%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: High-quality asset-light CRO, moat 6/10 — TTM owner's earnings $23.83/share and a raised guide, but at $613.74 the weighted IRR is only 10.8% (IV@15% $379); it clears the 15% hurdle only at or below ~$379.
moat_for: Full-service integration (design, labs, data, FDA filing under one roof) small biotechs cannot replicate in-house
Mid-trial CRO switching carries real operational and regulatory risk for sponsors
Scientific/regulatory depth in oncology, metabolic and CNS; high repeat-business rate
Asset-light, negative-working-capital model — net DSO -59.6 days, customers fund operations
Operating margin ~21% vs ~15-18% peer CRO EBITDA margins
moat_against: ~5% market share vs IQVIA (~19%) and ICON (~10%) with far greater scale and data assets
Project-based contracts — no recurring lock-in once a trial ends
Client concentration: top 5 ~31%, top 10 ~40% of LTM revenue
Customer base overwhelmingly small/mid biotech — hostage to funding cycles
